status_meaning.KEEP: carries information that survived our tests; carry forward to the large datasets
status_meaning.WATCH: some information but not enough to use alone; retest with more data or other markets
status_meaning.DROP: tested and found no usable information; do not carry forward

variables.name: Coin daily trend: close vs 50-day and 20-day averages
variables.evidence: Portfolio layer T3: halves drawdown vs buy-and-hold in 2017-23 and 2024-26; stable for 40/15 to 100/20 averages
variables.carry_forward: Core variable for every market: per-instrument trend state

variables.name: Market gate: BTC daily close vs its 50-day average
variables.evidence: T2/T3 beat T1 on drawdown and MAR; LUNA crash 0% vs -56%; study v4 also found the BTC gate reduced losses
variables.carry_forward: Generalise to 'market-wide gate' per market (index trend for stocks: Nifty, TSX, S&P 500)

variables.name: Exit bells in slow crashes (disaster stop, trend-break exit)
variables.evidence: Saved $2,365 across May 2021, LUNA, FTX, Oct 2025; cost money in V-shaped rebounds (COVID, Aug 2024)
variables.carry_forward: Crash insurance: keep, and measure per market with crisis replays

variables.name: Trading costs: fee + half-spread per instrument
variables.evidence: Every short-horizon rule failed on costs, not direction (round trip about 0.6-1.2% at NDAX); expensive coins lose more
variables.carry_forward: First-class variable: measured spreads per instrument and venue, refreshed monthly

variables.name: Entry order type: resting limit vs market
variables.evidence: Market entry significantly worse than limits (t -3.6 / -3.0); limit saves about 0.26% per trade
variables.carry_forward: Default to limits; never trust 'missed order' shadows as evidence (hindsight bias)

variables.name: Holding horizon (multi-week exposure)
variables.evidence: Random 60-day holds earned like our setups' holds (+$32 vs +$33 per $100 in 2017-23): return comes from being in up-trends
variables.carry_forward: Horizon is a decision variable; compare every rule against random entries at the same horizon

variables.name: Dip in a coin while BTC is bullish (15m RSI < 30, coin BEAR, BTC BULL)
variables.evidence: RSI15<30 beat random short-term entries by about $0.10 per trade in 2017-23 (t 3.9) but loses after costs; E6|BEAR|BTC BULL slightly positive gross in both periods (+0.17% / +0.07%)
variables.carry_forward: Retest on low-cost venues and on stocks (relative dips vs index)

variables.name: 4h trend filter for intraday entries
variables.evidence: Largest gross improvement in MTF entry study v1 (-0.039% to +0.005% per trade) but far below costs
variables.carry_forward: Useful as a context tag, not as an edge by itself

variables.name: Other traders' entry timing (Hyperliquid)
variables.evidence: +0.06% excess in the first hour (t 2.9), nothing later; skill did not persist from first to second half
variables.carry_forward: Reference only; revisit with order-flow data (who is aggressive, size)

variables.name: Buy strength vs buy weakness (traders' context)
variables.evidence: Traders' longs did better buying weakness (BEAR +0.67% vs BULL -0.41% 24h excess) but this did not survive being traded
variables.carry_forward: Candidate for stocks, where mean reversion is better documented

variables.name: Consecutive green 5m candles (2-5)
variables.evidence: After green runs the next candle is slightly less likely green (46.5% to 44.8% vs 47.9%); 0 of 67,167 cells pass; 15-60 min moves smaller than costs

variables.name: 15m/30m reversal crossings (S3)
variables.evidence: Confirmed vs early reversals flip sign between periods; confirmation does not help
variables.carry_forward: Do not carry forward as a signal; keep as a descriptive tag

variables.name: 1h market bias S1 (EMA50) for intraday entries
variables.evidence: No stable difference between BULL and BEAR entries in either period

variables.name: Volatility contraction (Bollinger width / ATR) and squeeze release
variables.evidence: Squeeze setup E5 worst in both periods; contraction tags carry no stable information

variables.name: Volume ratio (candle volume vs 20-candle average)
variables.evidence: No stable effect as a confirmation (green-run study, breakout setup)
variables.carry_forward: Replace with better volume data (taker buy/sell split)

variables.name: Warning bells (X3) in normal times
variables.evidence: Neither help nor hurt on average; removing them worsened crisis losses
variables.carry_forward: Keep as insurance; revisit sizing instead
